On receipt of the present Petition, the Bid Process Coordinator (hereinafter referred to as “BPC”), REC Power Development and Consultancy Limited (hereinafter referred to as “RECPDCL”), vide letter dated 20.3.2025, was directed to submit the relevant documents regarding the complete process of competitive bidding. The necessary details have been filed by the BPC vide affidavit dated 7.4.2025. 3. Vide Record of Proceedings (hereinafter referred to as “RoP”) dated 30.4.2025, notice was issued to the Respondents to file their respective replies. Thereafter, on 29.5.2025, the Commission observed that the discovered tariff in the present case is approximately 14.84% higher than the tariff computed in accordance with the prevailing norms, based on the estimated project cost as communicated by the Cost Committee. The Commission further noted that in its order dated 14.1.2025 in Petition No. 340/TL/2024, it had observed that: _‘since there are substantial financial implications on the beneficiaries at large, when the bid price is substantially higher than the estimated price, there is a need to consider the same based on an objective criterion to be issued in the public domain. We are of the view that a procedure in this regard specifying the objective criterion based on which re-bidding is finalised, is required to be put in place by the BPC along with the BEC after consulting the necessary stakeholders. Accordingly, the BPC is directed to finalise the procedure within a period of three months from the issue of this order for future cases.’_ 5. In response to the RoP dated 29.5.2025, BPC, i.e., RECPDCL, vide affidavit dated 12.6.2025, has submitted that the matter regarding finalization of an objective procedure, as directed by the Commission, is presently under active deliberation and consideration by the BPC in coordination with the Bid Evaluation Committee (BEC), and in consultation with various stakeholders, including the Central Electricity Authority (CEA). It is stated that the purpose of the ongoing consultation process is to evolve a fair, transparent, and technically robust framework that appropriately balances competitive bidding outcomes with the interests of the end beneficiaries. The draft framework is stated to be under development and is presently being refined based on stakeholder feedback. Accordingly, BPC has submitted that efforts are being made to finalise the said procedure/guidelines at the earliest possible and to place the same in the public domain for application in future cases, in compliance with the Commission’s directions. 7. We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner and BPC and perused the documents available on record. Section 63 of the Act provides as under: (c) The BPC shall prepare the bid documents in accordance with the Guidelines and obtain approval of the Appropriate Government, or alternatively, the BPC can use the Standard Bid Documents notified by the Ministry of Power. Any material deviation from the Standard Bidding Documents shall be made only with the prior approval of the Appropriate Government. Intimation about initiation of the bidding process shall be sent by the BPC to the Appropriate Commission. (k) BPC shall make the final result of evaluation of all bids public. The final TSA, along with the certification by the bid evaluation committee, shall be forwarded to the Appropriate Commission for the adoption of tariff discovered from the quoted annual transmission charges during the e-reverse bidding process in terms of Section 63 of the Act. 9. Therefore, we have to examine whether the Guidelines issued by the Central Government have been followed in the present case in a transparent process of bidding. 21. The Letter of Intent (hereinafter referred to as “LoI”) was issued by the BPC on 6.1.2025 to the successful bidder, i.e., Power Grid Corporation of India Limited. In accordance with Clause 12.3 of the Guidelines, the BPC has hosted on the website of RECPDCL the final result of the evaluation of the bids for the selection of a developer for the Project. 22. In accordance with the provisions of the bid documents and upon the issuance of LoI to the successful bidder (Power Grid Corporation of India Limited) and acquisition of SPV (the Petitioner) by the successful bidder, the Petitioner has prayed for the adoption of transmission charges for the Project which has been discovered through the competitive bidding process. 23.
